tasks.label: Upgrade city
tasks.description: Checks the Builder's Hut, then keeps both builders on the ticked buildings, top first, upgrading what each needs first. Never gems.

params.label: Buildings, in priority order
params.heading: Buildings, in priority order
params.help: Ticked buildings are upgraded from the top down, one per free builder. Each one's requirements are upgraded first.

params.label: Use Quick Replenish when short of resources
params.heading: Short of resources
params.help: Tops the shortfall up from resource items in storage. Never gems. Off: that building waits.

tasks.label: Research
tasks.description: Keeps the Academy researching, in the groups and order set: gathering speed, gem gathering, troop load, production, research and building speed, Military up to T4, the rest. Never gems.

params.label: Research, in priority order
params.heading: Research, in priority order
params.help: The first ticked line with something to research decides; move lines up or down, tick or untick any. Gathering speed is food, wood, stone and gold on the map; production speed is what the Farm, Lumber Mill, Quarry and Goldmine make. With both gem lines unticked, gem research is never done. 'Unlock more' researches whatever opens the next locked tech of that kind. Military up to T4 only opens Long Swordsman, Chu-Ko-Nu, Knight and Ballista.

params.label: Use Quick Replenish when short of resources
params.heading: Short of resources
params.help: Tops the shortfall up from resource items in storage. Never gems. Off: it waits for the resources.

tasks.label: Keep troops training
tasks.description: Trains a full batch in each idle troop building, at the tier set for it. Never INSTANT, never gems.

params.label: Barracks (infantry)
params.heading: Train
params.help: Train in this building when it is idle.

params.label: Tier
params.heading: Train
params.help: Which tier. A tier not unlocked yet trains the highest one below it.

params.label: Archery Range (archers)
params.heading: Train
params.help: Train in this building when it is idle.

params.label: Tier
params.heading: Train
params.help: Which tier. A tier not unlocked yet trains the highest one below it.

params.label: Stable (cavalry)
params.heading: Train
params.help: Train in this building when it is idle.

params.label: Tier
params.heading: Train
params.help: Which tier. A tier not unlocked yet trains the highest one below it.

params.label: Siege Workshop (siege)
params.heading: Train
params.help: Train in this building when it is idle.

params.label: Tier
params.heading: Train
params.help: Which tier. A tier not unlocked yet trains the highest one below it.

tasks.label: Collect blacksmith and produce
tasks.description: Takes whatever the blacksmith has finished, then sets it making more of the material you pick below.

params.label: Start producing after collecting
params.heading: Production
params.help: Untick to only collect the finished item and leave the forge idle.

params.label: Material
params.heading: Produce which
params.help: Which material to produce. 'Highest one' reads the four amounts and picks whichever you hold most of.

tasks.label: Claim VIP chest
tasks.description: Claims whichever VIP chests are on offer, from the badge at the top left. Once a day for each character, counted from 00:00 UTC.

tasks.label: Claim alliance resource
tasks.description: Claims the resources your alliance's territory has earned. Says so and stops when there is nothing waiting.

tasks.label: Donate technology
tasks.description: Reads the six skills' progress bars and donates to the ones that are not full yet, least full first, until the day's chances run out. Only ever the resource button, never the gem one beside it.

tasks.label: Buy from the merchant
tasks.description: Buys out the Mysterious Merchant in the Courier Station, all four rows, then takes the free refresh and buys again. Resource prices only - gem-priced stock is skipped and gem prompts get No.

tasks.label: Collect resource in city
tasks.description: Collects the Gold, Stone, Wood and Food waiting in your city. One click empties every building of a type, so the job is four clicks.

tasks.label: Travel from Dispatch
tasks.description: Opens the Dispatch building, takes the third icon to reach TRAVEL, and spends the day's chances down to none - as many at a time as the button offers. Once a day, since one visit empties them. Never gems.

tasks.label: Collect Expedition
tasks.description: Presses U for Campaign, opens Expedition and collects the chest beside the stage map. Once a day. Never Challenge, never the Expedition shop.

tasks.label: Claim Daily Objectives
tasks.description: Opens the quest scroll on the left, presses CLAIM on every finished Daily Objective and opens every activity chest the points have reached. Once a day. Never GO.

params.label: h UTC
params.heading: End of the UTC day
params.help: Claimed at the end of the UTC day, when the day's objectives are done: not before this hour (UTC). 19 leaves five hours - room for at least one cycle of three and a half.

tasks.label: Farm alliance gold
tasks.description: Sends one march to the alliance gold mother lode, known by its own nameplate so an ordinary gold mine is never mistaken for it, and only while the march queue has room. With R4 on, puts a new lode up by the marker when it has gone, capped at 100k per troop.

params.label: Send
params.heading: March
params.help: The saved troop preset sent to the alliance gold mother lode - and, with the R4 option below, the one that builds a new lode. If that march is not in the game, no preset is picked and the troops already loaded go instead.

params.label: R4: build a new mother lode if it is gone
params.heading: R4
params.help: When the marker is there but the lode is not, put a new one up: Alliance > Territory > Alliance Resource Center > Alliance Mother Lode, placed by the marker on the nearest clear ground, and the march picked above sent to build it. It costs the alliance 375K gold, and only an R4 account is offered the BUILD at all. A new lode is set to take at most 100,000 per troop, so one march cannot fill it alone.

tasks.label: Build 1 troop
tasks.description: Sends one troop to the alliance fortress once a day, with the march you pick, then checks every run and brings it home the moment its own building credit reaches 20,000. With R4 on, returns every member's troop that is full too.

params.label: Send
params.heading: March
params.help: The saved troop preset this sends to the fortress. They are numbered by you in the game, and need not start at 1 - one account here has 1, 2 and 7. If that march is not in the game, no preset is picked and the troops already loaded go instead.

params.label: R4: also return members' troops at 20,000
params.heading: R4
params.help: Only acts on an account whose fortress popup shows the purple R4 flag. Reads every member's Individual Credit in the BUILD list and returns the troops at exactly 20,000 - nobody else's. Runs with each cycle, like the other tasks; troops still under 20,000 wait for the next cycle.

tasks.label: Farm resource
tasks.description: Searches for resource nodes and sends gathering marches until the march queue is full.

params.label: Search for
params.heading: Search for
params.help: Which node type to search for. 'Highest one' farms whichever you hold most of; 'Lowest resource' whichever you hold least of, and 'except gold' leaves gold out of that.

params.label: Start level
params.heading: Node level
params.help: The node level searched first. Above what the game offers, it starts at the highest there is.

params.label: Lowest level
params.heading: Node level
params.help: When a level has nothing free, the search goes one level down, as far as this.

tasks.label: Assist resources
tasks.description: Sends resources to another city: ASSIST on the city at the coordinates below, one bar dragged all the way right, Transport - and again, until that resource runs out. Runs alone, on the current character only.

params.label: Send
params.heading: Send which
params.help: Which bar to fill. 'Highest one' fills whichever you hold most of, read again before every transport, and goes on to the next when that one runs out. A resource counts as run out when a full drag loads less than 1,000,000.

settings.label: Characters
settings.heading: Characters
settings.help: Every ticked task runs for each character in turn: the city work, then farming, then on to the next character.

settings.label: Repeat after waiting
settings.heading: Timer
settings.help: When every character has been through, wait and run the whole thing again, until you press Stop.

settings.label: h
settings.heading: Timer
settings.help: Shortest gap between runs. Each cycle waits a random time between this and the maximum.

settings.label: min
settings.heading: Timer
settings.help: Shortest gap between runs.

settings.label: h
settings.heading: Timer
settings.help: Longest gap between runs. A fresh wait is drawn for every cycle, so the schedule is never the same twice.

settings.label: min
settings.heading: Timer
settings.help: Longest gap between runs.

settings.label: Start from
settings.heading: Active hours
settings.help: Wait until this time before doing anything. A time that has already gone today does not wait for tomorrow - it starts straight away.

settings.label: h
settings.heading: Active hours
settings.help: When the panel may start working, on the local clock.

settings.label: min
settings.heading: Active hours
settings.help: When the panel may start working, on the local clock.

settings.label: End at
settings.heading: Active hours
settings.help: Stop when this time comes round. The character in progress finishes first, rather than stopping mid-march. With the repeat timer on, the next cycle waits for the start time.

settings.label: h
settings.heading: Active hours
settings.help: When it stops, on the local clock.

settings.label: min
settings.heading: Active hours
settings.help: When it stops, on the local clock.

choices: Both - the first, then the second
settings.label: Run
settings.heading: Run which game
settings.help: Both: when the first game has had its cycle, it is closed, the second is started and the same tasks run there for its characters; before the next cycle the second is closed and the first started again. Without a second game set, this is always the first.

settings.label: Start a game if it is not running
settings.heading: Both games
settings.help: For whichever game a cycle runs on - the first, the second or both in turn. Checked before every cycle; needs its path above. The panel waits for the game to finish loading before it does anything. With both games run, each is started in turn whatever this says.

settings.label: Close the game while waiting for the timer
settings.heading: Both games
settings.help: For whichever game the cycle ended on: shut it down for the wait and start it again for the next cycle. Only does anything with the timer on.

settings.label: Report days in
settings.heading: Report time zone
settings.help: Which clock the daily report and the Summary tab count their days by. UTC is where the game's day rolls over. Days already recorded keep the day they were filed under.

settings.label: days
settings.heading: Keep history for
settings.help: How many days of logs, saved reports and recorded totals to keep under the source folder. Older files are deleted as new ones are written.

settings.label: Always start as administrator
settings.heading: Startup
settings.help: The game runs elevated, and Windows refuses input sent to it from a normal process. With this on, the panel asks for administrator rights the moment it opens, instead of you noticing the warning banner and restarting it by hand.

settings.label: After the run
settings.heading: Screen off
settings.help: Turn the screen off when a run finishes. If it could not go off then - a video or sound was playing - it tries again after x, until it has. With 'Every x' as well, it then goes off again every x.

settings.label: Every x
settings.heading: Screen off
settings.help:
Turn the screen off every x through the wait between cycles, so a notification that lights it at two in the morning does not leave it on until dawn. Without 'After the run', the first time is x after the run finishes.
Either way it comes back on by itself two minutes before the next cycle, and it is never turned off while a video or sound is playing.

settings.label: x
settings.heading: Screen off
settings.help: Every x: how often the screen is turned off again. After the run: how long to wait before trying again if it did not go off.

settings.label: Hibernate until the next cycle
settings.heading: Screen off
settings.help: Between cycles, put the machine into hibernation and let a wake timer bring it back a couple of minutes before the next one. On a laptop whose screen-off means Modern Standby this is the only way cycles keep running unattended - measured here, nothing in software wakes Modern Standby, while hibernation wakes on its timer every time. Skipped for short waits, while the machine is in use, and when the power plan ignores wake timers (it does on battery by default).

settings.label: Keep awake until the next run
settings.heading: Screen off
settings.help: Between cycles, keep the machine and the screen on - no hibernation, no screen-off, no sleep - until the next cycle starts. The surest way for cycles to run unattended, at the price of a lit screen and no saving of power. Takes the place of 'Hibernate until the next cycle' and of the Screen off settings above while it is on.

same_as_high.label: Same tasks as Hall 24+
same_as_high.help: Run Lower Hall characters with the tasks ticked on Hall 24+. Lower Hall's own ticks are kept, greyed out, for when this is off. Its options - the resource to farm, the buildings to upgrade - are still its own.
